items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: I think what Wynton is doing with his jazz education and his spreading the Gospel... That’s been very helpful.

ctx.x: Is the way those fellows played teachable do you think?

I think so. I think it is. I think it’s like a language, it’s like learning a foreign language. But you have to have a willing student and someone who is not afraid of being criticized about learning that style. And a lot of young people today, you know, they want to be with it, and they want to be where the rest of their musicians are thinking. And if you want to stray a little bit out of that it’s really hard. I can tell youth from that being from my youth. I think it’s a lot possibly easier today. I think what…
It’s interesting, tomorrow morning there’s a panel entitled “Trad Jazz, Alive and Well.” Should be an interesting conversation.
